questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: The Earth's polar diameter is shorter than its equatorial diameter mainly because of the
options: absorption of solar energy by the atmosphere
gravitational pull of the Moon on the oceans
flattening of the poles caused by the Earth's rotation
revolution of the Earth around the Sun
questions.explanation: The Earth rotates rapidly, producing an equatorial bulge and polar flattening, so its polar diameter is shorter. The Moon's gravitational pull mainly produces tides, while the Earth's revolution and solar heating do not determine its shape.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: The Moon always presents almost the same face to the Earth because the Moon
options: takes the same time to rotate on its axis as it takes to revolve around the Earth
revolves around the Earth in the same time that the Earth rotates on its axis
does not rotate on its axis at all
has an orbit that is perfectly circular around the Earth
questions.explanation: The Moon is in synchronous rotation: one rotation on its axis takes about the same period as one revolution around the Earth. If it did not rotate, observers on Earth would see all sides of the Moon over time.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: The main asteroid belt in the solar system lies between the orbits of
questions.explanation: Most asteroids occupy a belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, where their orbits are strongly influenced by Jupiter. The other pairs do not contain the main asteroid belt.

questions.q: A small settlement consisting of a cluster of farmsteads with no church, school or market is best described as a
questions.explanation: A hamlet is a very small rural settlement, often just a few farmsteads, and it lacks major services such as a market, school or church. A village generally has more dwellings and some basic services, while towns and cities are larger and more developed.

questions.q: A settlement on the outskirts of Abuja where most residents travel to the city for work each morning and return in the evening is functioning mainly as a
questions.explanation: A dormitory settlement provides homes for people who work elsewhere, so many residents commute daily to Abuja. A central business district is a commercial core, a primate city dominates an urban system, and a rural market centre serves local trading needs.

questions.q: Soft-drink bottling plants in Nigeria are often located close to their markets mainly because the product is
options: perishable and must be consumed immediately
bulky and expensive to transport over long distances
made from very rare raw materials
highly valuable and easy to transport
questions.explanation: Soft drinks contain a large proportion of water, making the bottled product heavy and bulky; transport costs rise sharply with distance, so production is market-oriented. They are not so perishable that they must be consumed immediately, and the raw materials are common.

questions.q: A pottery factory is located close to a clay deposit in Abeokuta mainly because clay is
options: a renewable resource that changes with weather
heavy and bulky, so transporting it is costly
questions.explanation: Clay is a weight-losing raw material used in large quantities, so making pottery near the deposit reduces transport costs. It is not found only in urban areas and is not especially valuable per unit weight compared with processed pottery.

questions.q: The wearing away of river-loaded rock fragments as they collide with one another and become smaller and rounder is called
questions.explanation: Attrition is the reduction of rock fragments through collisions with one another in the river channel. Abrasion is the grinding of the river bed and banks, hydraulic action is the force of water, and solution is chemical removal.

questions.q: A crescent-shaped sand dune formed by wind deposition in a desert is called a
questions.explanation: A barchan is a crescent-shaped dune built by wind deposition, with horns pointing downwind. Yardangs and zeugens are erosional desert features, while an inselberg is a residual hill.

questions.q: A mineral specimen obtained from a pegmatite near Ibadan can be split into thin, flexible, transparent sheets and is used as an electrical insulator. Which mineral is it?
questions.explanation: Muscovite mica has a sheet-like cleavage and can be split into thin, flexible, transparent sheets, which makes it useful as an electrical insulator. Quartz is hard and does not split into flexible sheets, while galena and haematite are metallic ores.

questions.q: A rock composed mainly of rounded sand grains cemented together by silica is called
questions.explanation: Sandstone is made of sand-sized grains, usually quartz, held together by a cementing material such as silica. Conglomerate may also contain rounded fragments, but its fragments are pebbles rather than sand grains.

questions.q: The Kainji Dam is built across which river?
questions.explanation: The Kainji Dam is located on the River Niger in Niger State. It is one of Nigeria's major hydro-electric power projects and also supports irrigation and fishing.

questions.q: Which Nigerian state has Abeokuta as its capital and shares an international boundary with the Republic of Benin?
questions.explanation: Abeokuta is the capital of Ogun State, and Ogun State lies along Nigeria's international boundary with the Republic of Benin. Lagos State also shares a boundary with Benin, but its capital is Ikeja, not Abeokuta.

questions.q: In overseas trade, which document serves as a receipt issued by the shipping company for goods loaded on board and can also act as a document of title?
questions.explanation: A bill of lading is issued by the shipping company to acknowledge that goods have been received or loaded for shipment. It also serves as evidence of the contract of carriage and may function as a document of title, unlike an invoice or certificate of origin.

questions.q: What is a major advantage of railway transport over road transport for long-distance haulage of bulky goods?
options: It is unaffected by fixed track maintenance.
It can carry larger quantities at a lower cost per tonne-kilometre.
questions.explanation: Rail transport is well suited to moving heavy and bulky goods over long distances because it has a low cost per tonne-kilometre and a high carrying capacity. Road transport is better for door-to-door service and route flexibility, while railways depend on fixed tracks and their maintenance.

questions.q: A map has a scale of 1:40,000. The distance between two villages on the map is 6.5 cm. What is the straight-line distance between the villages on the ground?
questions.explanation: Using the scale, 6.5 cm on the map represents 6.5 × 40,000 cm = 260,000 cm on the ground. Since 100,000 cm = 1 km, the ground distance is 2.6 km.

questions.q: A rectangular school field measures 4.5 cm by 2.8 cm on a map with scale 1:20,000. What is its actual area in hectares?
questions.explanation: At 1:20,000, 1 cm represents 20,000 cm or 200 m. The actual sides are 4.5 × 200 = 900 m and 2.8 × 200 = 560 m, so the area is 900 × 560 = 504,000 m². Dividing by 10,000 m² per hectare gives 50.4 hectares.

questions.q: Which description of a population pyramid indicates a very young and rapidly growing population?
options: A narrow base with a wide top
A large bulge in the middle with a very small base
Nearly the same width at all age groups
A broad base that narrows sharply towards the top
questions.explanation: A broad base shows a large proportion of children, while the sharp narrowing indicates high death rates at older ages, typical of a young and rapidly growing population. A narrow base with a wide top would indicate an ageing or declining population.

questions.q: A farmer in Bali LGA, Taraba State, clears a plot, crops it for two years, then leaves it to regain fertility while farming a new plot. This farming practice is called
questions.explanation: Shifting cultivation involves cultivating a plot for a few years and then leaving it to fallow while a new plot is cleared. Crop rotation keeps the same land in continuous use but changes the crops grown.

questions.q: Which soil layer is usually richest in humus and most directly supports crop roots?
questions.explanation: The topsoil is the surface layer where humus accumulates and where most crop roots and soil organisms are concentrated. The subsoil and deeper layers contain fewer nutrients and less organic matter.

questions.q: Why do tropical rainforest soils in southern Nigeria often lose fertility soon after the forest is cleared?
options: A thick humus layer remains unchanged for many years after clearing.
Most nutrients are locked up in the parent rock and are never released.
Rainfall is too low to decompose the fallen leaves.
Organic matter breaks down rapidly and nutrients are quickly leached or removed with crops.
questions.explanation: High temperatures and heavy rainfall cause rapid decomposition of litter and strong leaching of released nutrients after forest clearance. In the undisturbed forest, most nutrients are held in the vegetation and cycling litter rather than stored in the soil.

questions.q: What mainly explains why montane vegetation is found on the Jos Plateau?
options: Rainfall is too low to support any trees.
The low altitude makes the area hotter than the surrounding plains.
The high altitude gives cooler temperatures than the surrounding lowlands.
The soil is permanently frozen beneath the surface.
questions.explanation: Altitude lowers temperature, so the Jos Plateau has cooler and often moister conditions than the surrounding lowlands. This helps produce vegetation different from the surrounding savanna.

questions.q: A community in Cross River State plants trees on cleared slopes and bans farming on very steep land. Which hazard are these measures mainly intended to control?
questions.explanation: Tree planting on cleared slopes and avoiding cultivation on very steep land reduce runoff and increase infiltration, thereby limiting soil erosion and gully growth. Such measures are not mainly aimed at tidal flooding, desert encroachment or factory air pollution.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of in-situ conservation?
options: Keeping rare animals in a city zoo
Protecting a natural forest reserve so species remain in their original habitat
Storing seeds in a refrigerated seed bank
Growing endangered plants only in a botanical garden
questions.explanation: In-situ conservation protects species within their natural habitat, as in a protected natural forest reserve. Zoos, seed banks and botanical gardens keep organisms outside their natural habitats and are examples of ex-situ conservation.

questions.q: Two points lie on the equator at longitudes 10°E and 40°E. What is the approximate shortest distance between them along the equator?
questions.explanation: The longitude difference is 40° − 10° = 30°. At the equator, 1° of longitude is approximately 111 km, so the shortest distance is 30 × 111 km = 3,330 km. The value 1,110 km would correspond to only one 10° interval.

questions.q: On a hot afternoon in Oyo, a farmer sees tall clouds developing and then experiences heavy rain lasting for a short time. Which type of rainfall is most likely occurring?
questions.explanation: Heating of the ground causes moist air to rise, cool and form towering cumulonimbus clouds, producing short but heavy convectional rain. Orographic rainfall requires air being forced up a mountain barrier, while frontal rainfall is associated with the meeting of contrasting air masses.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Which observation best supports the description of the Earth as an oblate spheroid?
options: The polar diameter is shorter than the equatorial diameter.
The Moon changes shape in a regular cycle.
The Earth revolves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit.
Day and night follow each other at regular intervals.
questions.explanation: An oblate spheroid is a sphere flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator, so its polar diameter is shorter than its equatorial diameter. The other observations are explained by revolution, lunar phases and rotation rather than by the Earth's shape.

questions.q: Which Nigerian town grew mainly because it is located at the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers?
questions.explanation: Lokoja is situated at the confluence of the Niger and Benue, a site that favoured trade, transport and administration at the meeting of river routes. Kano grew mainly from trans-Saharan trade, Enugu from coal mining, and Ibadan from its military and agricultural hinterland.

questions.q: A student in Katsina observes Polaris at about 13° above the northern horizon. Which latitude is most likely for Katsina?
questions.explanation: In the Northern Hemisphere, the altitude of Polaris above the horizon is approximately equal to the observer's latitude. Since Katsina is north of the equator and Polaris is seen 13° above the northern horizon, its latitude is about 13°N. A latitude of 26°N would make Polaris appear about 26° high.

questions.q: Which statement best explains why the maximum air temperature at Ilorin is usually recorded in the early afternoon rather than at noon?
options: The ground continues to release heat to the air after maximum sunshine.
Air pressure is highest at that time.
The Sun is directly overhead at that time.
Relative humidity is highest at that time.
questions.explanation: Although insolation is strongest around noon, the ground takes time to absorb heat and then transfer it to the air by conduction and convection. Air temperature therefore continues to rise until the ground's heat output to the atmosphere begins to fall, giving a maximum in the early afternoon. The Sun is not generally directly overhead at that time.

questions.q: Which of these is a low-order service that a small village is most likely to provide?
options: A primary school and a weekly market
questions.explanation: Small villages normally provide low-order services that require a small threshold population, such as a primary school and a weekly market. Specialist teaching hospitals, central bank branches and international airports need much larger populations and are found in higher-order settlements.

questions.q: At a certain place, the local solar time is 15:00 when it is 12:00 noon at Greenwich. What is the longitude of the place?
questions.explanation: The place is 3 hours ahead of Greenwich. Since the Earth turns 15° of longitude per hour, a 3-hour difference corresponds to 3 × 15° = 45°. A place ahead of Greenwich time lies east, so the longitude is 45°E; 45°W would be 3 hours behind Greenwich.

questions.q: A company plans to invest ₦2 billion in a tomato paste factory in Kano close to the Kano River irrigation project. Which factor is most important in the choice of this location?
questions.explanation: Tomatoes are bulky and perishable, so processing them near the irrigation schemes reduces spoilage and transport costs. A seaport is not needed for obtaining local tomatoes, while skilled labour and coal are less decisive for this type of factory.

questions.q: An aluminium smelting firm in Nigeria is sited beside a gas-fired power station. Which advantage is it mainly seeking?
options: Nearness to a major market for aluminium
Availability of limestone as a flux
questions.explanation: Aluminium smelting uses electrolysis and therefore consumes very large amounts of electricity; a nearby gas-fired station provides a steady and relatively cheap power supply. Bauxite may be transported to the smelter, but the dominant locational pull is electric power.

questions.q: Which of the following activities around Bonny is a primary industry?
options: Refining of crude oil into petrol
Filling of cooking gas into cylinders
questions.explanation: Primary industries extract raw materials directly from the earth or sea, and crude oil extraction is an example. Refining, filling gas cylinders and making plastic buckets involve manufacturing or processing, so they are secondary activities.

questions.q: The chemical removal of soluble rock by river water is known as
questions.explanation: Solution occurs when river water dissolves minerals from rocks such as limestone and carries them away in solution. Attrition is the wearing away of load by collision, hydraulic action is the force of moving water, and saltation is the bouncing transport of particles.

questions.q: Which process most directly produces exfoliation on exposed granite surfaces during hot days and cool nights?
options: Repeated expansion and contraction of the outer rock layer
Grinding of rock by wind-blown sand
Reaction of rainwater with calcium carbonate
Freezing of water in cracks and joints
questions.explanation: In hot, dry conditions the outer layer of granite expands by day and contracts at night, weakening and peeling off in sheets. Freezing water causes frost shattering, calcium carbonate reacts in carbonation, and wind-blown sand causes abrasion rather than exfoliation.

questions.q: The way a mineral breaks along definite flat planes is known as
questions.explanation: Cleavage is the tendency of a mineral to split along flat planes related to its internal atomic structure. Fracture is an irregular break, streak is the colour of a mineral's powder, and lustre is its surface appearance in reflected light.

questions.q: A fine-grained metamorphic rock that splits easily into thin sheets used for roofing is called
questions.explanation: Slate forms from shale under heat and pressure and has slaty cleavage, allowing it to be split into thin roofing sheets. Marble and quartzite are also metamorphic rocks but are not used in thin sheets, while basalt is an igneous rock.

questions.q: Cement production at Nkalagu, using nearby limestone, is associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Nkalagu, where limestone deposits support cement production, is located in Ebonyi State. Ogun, Kogi and Sokoto also have important cement plants, but Nkalagu is specifically associated with Ebonyi State.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:75,000, the distance between two settlements is 12.6 cm. What is the straight-line distance between the settlements on the ground?
questions.explanation: At 1:75,000, 1 cm on the map represents 75,000 cm on the ground, which is 0.75 km. Therefore 12.6 cm represents 12.6 × 0.75 km = 9.45 km. The value 0.945 km results from an error in converting centimetres to kilometres.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:25,000, a rectangular farm measures 6.8 cm by 4.2 cm. What is the actual area of the farm?
questions.explanation: At 1:25,000, 1 cm represents 25,000 cm or 0.25 km. The ground dimensions are 6.8 × 0.25 = 1.7 km and 4.2 × 0.25 = 1.05 km, so the area is 1.7 × 1.05 = 1.785 km². The value 7.14 km² is obtained by an incorrect area conversion.

questions.q: A town had a mid-year population of 80,000. During the year, there were 2,400 live births, 900 deaths, 1,100 immigrants and 500 emigrants. What was the population at the end of the year?
questions.explanation: Natural increase is 2,400 − 900 = 1,500 persons, while net migration is 1,100 − 500 = 600 persons. The total increase is 1,500 + 600 = 2,100 persons, so the end-of-year population is 80,000 + 2,100 = 82,100. The value 81,500 omits net migration.

questions.q: A country has a total population of 180 million. Of this, 72 million are below 15 years and 18 million are aged 65 years and above. What is the dependency ratio per 100 working-age persons?
questions.explanation: The working-age population is 180 − 72 − 18 = 90 million. The dependent population is 72 + 18 = 90 million. Thus the dependency ratio is (90 ÷ 90) × 100 = 100 dependants per 100 working-age persons.

questions.q: A farmer applies 200 kg of NPK fertilizer grade 20:10:10 to one hectare of maize. How many kilograms of actual nitrogen are supplied to that hectare?
questions.explanation: The grade 20:10:10 means the fertilizer contains 20% nitrogen. The actual nitrogen supplied is therefore (20 ÷ 100) × 200 = 40 kg. The value 80 kg would result from wrongly adding the three nutrient percentages together.

questions.q: A trader in Aba needs to send a small, high-value parcel of urgently needed machine spare parts to a buyer in Kano within a few hours. Which mode of transport is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Air transport is the fastest mode for small, high-value and very urgent consignments over long inland distances. Sea transport cannot serve Kano directly, rail transport is generally slower and less flexible for small urgent parcels, and pipelines are suitable only for fluids or gases.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of invisible trade for Nigeria?
options: Payment for banking and insurance services supplied to another country
Export of crude oil to Asia
Export of tin ore to Europe
Export of cocoa beans to Europe
questions.explanation: Invisible trade refers to international trade in services rather than tangible goods. Banking and insurance services sold abroad earn foreign exchange without exporting physical commodities. Cocoa beans, crude oil and tin ore are visible exports because they are physical goods.

questions.q: The natural vegetation found along the fresh-water creeks and floodplains of the Niger Delta, where the water is not salty, is best described as
questions.explanation: Fresh-water swamp forest develops where river channels and floodplains carry abundant fresh water with little salt. Mangrove forest is restricted mainly to brackish and saline tidal flats, while Sudan savanna and montane grassland occur in much drier or higher locations.

questions.q: In soil texture classification, the soil particles that are less than 0.002 mm in diameter are called
questions.explanation: Clay particles are the finest soil separates, with a diameter smaller than 0.002 mm. Silt and sand particles are larger, while gravel consists of coarse fragments; these coarser materials give quicker drainage and less cohesion.

questions.q: In some Nigerian savanna soils, alternating wet and dry seasons cause iron compounds to move downward and harden in the subsoil. The resulting hard layer is called
questions.explanation: An iron pan forms when iron compounds are leached downward during wet periods and then become cemented on drying. A salt pan is formed by accumulation of salts, while humus and mulch are surface organic materials and do not form a hardened iron-rich subsoil layer.

questions.q: A fast-growing town in Niger State is repeatedly flooded because houses have been built on the floodplain of a river. Which measure is most sustainable for reducing the hazard in future?
options: raising all buildings on taller concrete pillars along the riverbank
covering the floodplain with concrete to speed water away
enforcing land-use zoning that keeps floodplains free of buildings
dredging the river once after each flood season
questions.explanation: Keeping floodplains free of buildings is preventive and sustainable because it allows rivers to flood naturally without damaging settlements. Raising buildings on pillars may still expose people and property to severe floods, while paving the floodplain or relying on occasional dredging does not remove the basic danger.

questions.q: A school in Enugu has a steep compound where rainwater has begun to wash away the topsoil. Which practice will most directly control the erosion?
options: removing all vegetation so that rainwater can flow freely
planting grass and constructing contour drains across the slope
digging a deep straight trench down the slope
paving the entire slope with smooth concrete
questions.explanation: Grass cover reduces the impact of raindrops and binds soil particles, while contour drains guide water across the slope and reduce its erosive speed. Removing vegetation, paving smooth surfaces, or cutting a straight downslope trench can increase runoff and deepen erosion.

questions.q: A weather observer at a Nigerian town records local solar time as 08:40 when Greenwich Mean Time is 08:20. What is the longitude of the town?
questions.explanation: The town is 20 minutes ahead of Greenwich; 20 ÷ 4 = 5° of longitude. Since local solar time is ahead of GMT, the town lies east of Greenwich, giving 5°E.

questions.q: Nigeria uses GMT+1. When the time in Lagos is 07:00, what is the time in a country that uses GMT+4?
questions.explanation: GMT+4 is three hours ahead of GMT+1, so the time there is 07:00 + 3 hours = 10:00. Subtracting the difference would give a time before Lagos, which is incorrect because places farther east in this example are ahead.

questions.q: Two towns experience solar noon at exactly the same moment. This is because the towns lie on the same
questions.explanation: Local solar noon occurs at the same moment for places on the same meridian, since they share the same longitude. Places on the same latitude or in the same standard time zone may still be at different longitudes and therefore may not reach solar noon together.

questions.q: The seasonal northward and southward migration of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone over Nigeria is chiefly caused by the
options: deflection of winds by the Coriolis force
influence of cold ocean currents along the coast
apparent movement of the sun between the Tropics
rotation of the earth on its axis
questions.explanation: The ITCZ follows the zone of greatest solar heating, so its seasonal shift reflects the apparent movement of the overhead sun between the Tropics. The Earth's rotation and the Coriolis force affect wind direction, but they do not cause this seasonal north–south migration.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: The equatorial belt is generally hotter than the polar regions mainly because the equatorial belt
options: is less affected by the Earth's rotation
receives more direct solar rays concentrated over a smaller surface area
is much closer to the Sun than the polar regions
has a longer period of daylight throughout the year
questions.explanation: At low latitudes the Sun's rays strike almost vertically, so the same amount of solar energy is concentrated over a smaller area; near the poles the rays are slanting and spread out. The Earth's distance from the Sun does not differ enough between the equator and the poles to cause the temperature difference.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: The apparent deflection of winds and ocean currents to the right in the Northern Hemisphere is mainly caused by the Earth's
questions.explanation: This deflection is the Coriolis effect, produced by the Earth's west-to-east rotation. Revolution and axial tilt are associated mainly with the seasons, while the Moon's gravity is the main cause of tides.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: A coastal town records high tide at 9.00 a.m. on Tuesday. When is the next high tide expected at the same place?
questions.explanation: The lunar day is about 24 hours 50 minutes, so successive high tides at the same place are about 12 hours 25 minutes apart. Adding this to 9.00 a.m. gives 9.25 p.m. on Tuesday; ignoring the extra 50 minutes leads to the incorrect 9.00 p.m. figure.

questions.q: The rapid growth of Abuja from a small settlement to a major city after 1976 was mainly stimulated by its
options: role as the seat of the federal government
location at the confluence of two major rivers
questions.explanation: Abuja's selection as Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory attracted government offices, workers, businesses and infrastructure, causing rapid urban growth. It was not a gold-mining centre, river confluence, or seaport.
